text:
Travis Sanheim plays 25 minutes a night for a Flyers team that is losing more than it wins, and he's the best reason to think their blue line is better than the record. Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.3 wins above replacement last season, 23rd among 215 defencemen, taking chances away against top competition and even drawing more penalties than he took (+3.1 goals from that alone).

This season the points are a little light, eight in 20 games, with two goals on 3.7 expected. The most recent was an empty-net, shorthanded goal in Vancouver on Monday, a long shot during six-on-four play that sealed the Flyers' 3-1 win. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why he can score more: he joins the rush, with 33% of his shots coming off it against a typical 17% for defencemen, and gets to the slot more than most. Philadelphia takes 46% of the expected goals with him on, better than without him. Our range has him around 36 points, and his shooting should pick up.
